stances.claim: Opening the SALNs to the public, as Remulla has done by Memorandum Circular No. 3, is a 'good start' that fulfills the constitutional, RA 6713, and RA 6770 mandates, but its real test lies in the reasonableness of the procedural guidelines balancing the right to know against the right to privacy under RA 10173.

The 'no earlier than 10 working days' floor for public access is too restrictive given modern reproduction technology and should be phased into a timetable (SALNs of the last 5 years available within -- not no-earlier-than -- 10 calendar days; 5-10 years within 20 days; and so on).
stances.rhetorical_move: preposition-as-substance critique ('within' vs 'no earlier than') + phased-timetable counter-proposal

stances.claim: Both the original and the corrected SALN, together with the declarant's reasons for the correction, should be public -- not only the corrected version -- because the corrections themselves are evidence of declarant conduct and possible cover-up.

The redactions (home address, minor children's identifying data, signature, government IDs) are reasonable on their face but must remain reversible: an applicant who shows specific need (e.g., evidence that a namesake spouse, ascendant, descendant, or relative is being used to hide ill-gotten wealth) should be granted access to the redacted portions.

RA 6713 is in fact stricter than the OMB guidelines -- it requires not only the SALN but also a separate Disclosure of Business Interests and Financial Connections, and full and faithful pre-existing compliance with it would already have prevented or 'moderated the greed' driving the pork-barrel and flood-control scams.

notable_anecdotes: President Marcos voluntarily released his own SALN even though, under the law, his consent is not required -- a quiet executive endorsement that gave the new OMB circular political cover on day one.

CJ flagging a single preposition ('no earlier than' vs 'within') as the difference between meaningful and tokenistic disclosure -- a lawyerly close-reading of the very guidelines he is otherwise praising.

The contention that RA 6713, passed long ago, is already stricter than the new OMB guidelines -- and that the country's scandals (pork barrel, flood control) are failures of implementation, not of legislation.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban offers a guarded welcome to Ombudsman Jesus Crispin 'Boying' Remulla's Memorandum Circular No. 3, Series of 2025, which opens public officials' SALNs to public inspection in fulfillment of the Constitution, RA 6713 (Ethical Standards Law) and RA 6770 (Ombudsman Law), while balancing them against RA 10173 (Data Privacy Law). He praises President Marcos and the lawmakers who voluntarily released their SALNs, but tests the circular guideline by guideline: he argues the 'no earlier than 10 working days' access floor should be replaced with a phased timetable in which SALNs filed in the last five years are available within ten calendar days; that both original and corrected SALNs (with the declarant's reasons) should be public, not only the corrected versions; that the redactions of home address, minor children's identifying data, signature and government IDs are reasonable but must remain rebuttable upon a showing of specific need; and that the welcome lifestyle-check provision should be vigorously used. He closes with the recurring series argument that RA 6713 -- which requires both a SALN and a separate Disclosure of Business Interests and Financial Connections -- is already stricter than the new guidelines, and that strict pre-existing compliance would have 'moderated the greed' behind the pork-barrel and flood-control scams.
